one_sentence_story: Originated by Mamie Phipps Clark and co-led with Kenneth B. Clark across 253 children aged 3–7 (1939–1950), the Four-Doll Experiment revealed how early young children absorb society's racial status hierarchy — providing key empirical evidence cited by the U.S. Supreme Court in Brown v. Board of Education (1954) to strike down legal school segregation.
so_what_for_you: Remember that preschoolers aged 3–6 are sharp detectives of cultural signals: surround children early with books, toys, and role models where every background shines, and speak openly and warmly so society's stereotypes never go unchallenged.
